title: Initial handoff notes — Elena Park (LLM Runtime candidate)
content:
Quick context and purpose:
This is a lightweight, first-pass handoff for Elena Park — interviewed for Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime. Use these notes as fodder for the debrief; they are rough and include my immediate gut + specifics to surface in follow-ups (tech deep-dive + a systems interview).

Interview panel (round 1):
- Rajesh Menon (runtime infra) — concurrency/throughput questions
- Sophie Chen (serving runtime) — quantization/latency tradeoffs
- Miguel Rivera (SRE) — reliability, failure modes, rollout safety
- Caitlin Huang (me) — systems design, product fit

Verdict (tentative): leaning toward move-forward to system-design loop, but schedule a focused quantization coding exercise first. Strong in debugging/ops instincts; weaker on async batching design details.

High level summary (2–3 lines):
Elena has solid production experience running LLM inference at scale (ex: built a multi-tenant inference service at previous company) and demonstrated practical knowledge of quantization toolchains. She is pragmatic about tradeoffs and has good incident-postmortem instincts. Gaps: some ambiguity in continuous-batching architecture and how she would handle head-of-line blocking in mixed-latency workloads.

Strengths observed:
- Operations-first mindset: concrete examples of incident triage, RCA ownership, and automations that reduced pager noise.
- Quantization experience: worked with PTQ flow for INT8 on both CPU and GPU; mentioned use of calibration sets and per-channel quantization to preserve accuracy for attention layers.
- Familiar with memory/KV cache strategies: described LRU-ish eviction with prefetched prefixes for hot sessions.
- Communication: clear, concise, good at surfacing assumptions.

Concerns / gaps:
- Continuous batching and latency SLAs: when pushed for architecture to preserve 99th% latency while batching, answer got fuzzy. She proposed batching windows but couldn't articulate prioritization preemption or fair scheduling across tenants.
- Limited exposure to kernel-level optimizations: more on system-level orchestration than custom kernels or fused-attention strategies. That may be okay for this role depending on level.
- Some hand-wavy parts around model variant fallbacks (how to gracefully degrade across quantized variants without visible regressions).

Concrete examples from interview:
- Incident story: described a production outage caused by stale KV cache metadata; she traced it to race during shard resharding and implemented a two-phase commit-ish fix plus a small rollout gating that prevented recurrence. Good ownership story.
- Quantization: showed a short write-up (sent beforehand) where she benchmarked per-channel INT8 vs PTQ with calibration, reported mean latency improvements ~1.6x and small quality delta on a summarization task. She used ONNX + Triton in the flow.
- Load-shedding idea: proposed a tiered routing policy (premium vs best-effort) with automatic model-fallbacks. Lacked detail on enforcement of latency SLO for best-effort traffic.

Suggested follow-ups / next interviews:
1) Hands-on quantization coding task (30–45m) — short lab: given a small transformer, demonstrate PTQ calibration and show tradeoffs in accuracy vs latency. Evaluate both CPU and GPU inference pathways.
2) Focused systems design (60m) — continuous batching across mixed latency tenants. Include: preemption, fair queuing, token-level batching windows, and cache-aware scheduling. Ask for a design doc sketch afterwards.
3) Optional: short kernel/optimization primer conversation with research-applied-ml if we consider a level with kernel-hacking expectations.

Suggested rubric / scoring (quick):
- Technical depth (runtime & infra): 3.5/5 — solid infra ops and integration knowledge; moderate depth on low-level performance hacks.
- Product-systems fit (rollouts, SLAs): 4/5 — very good at operational controls and incremental rollouts.
- Coding/algorithmic: 3/5 — competent; fine for a senior infra engineer but maybe not for Staff-level kernel work.
- Communication & ownership: 5/5 — excellent.

Notes to interviewers for debrief:
- Push for concrete preemption/fairness strategies in the next round. Specifically ask how Elena would design a scheduler that can respect per-request latency budgets while still batching for throughput.
- Ask how she would validate model-fallback quality (automated eval suites, synthetic prompts, canary traffic percentage, rollback thresholds).
- Confirm comfort level with Triton/OpenVINO/ONNX runtimes — she mentioned Triton primarily; check GPU micro-ops familiarity if we need kernel-level work.

Admin/other:
- Candidate timezone: PST (open to reloc/can work remote).
- Salary expectations: gave a band that aligns with our senior range (verbal).
- Availability: 2–3 weeks notice.

My recommendation (short):
Run the quantization lab + systems design interview. If both are acceptable, move to an on-site loop (or virtual full loop) with an emphasis on scheduling and fallback strategies. I think she is a strong cultural/ops fit and has the potential to own production runtime features quickly.

Open questions I still have (to resolve in debrief):
- How deep is her familiarity with Triton custom backends / creating optimized CUDA kernels?
- Does she have experience with model-agnostic fallback policies (e.g., real-time quality gating) or were those more conceptual?
- Confirm past team structure: was she the primary owner of inference infra or a contributor within a larger infra eng org?

Scratch todo (my items):
- Add scoring matrix from Sophie & Rajesh after their notes in comments.
- Draft quantization lab prompt and share with candidate scheduling.
- Create JIRA follow-up: JIRA-RT-4123 (interview loop tasks).

End of notes.
